question: What did Nvidia announce about its Blackwell Ultra and Rubin chips in 2025?
text:
At **GTC on March 18, 2025**, Nvidia unveiled **Blackwell Ultra** as its near-term AI chip upgrade and laid out the roadmap for **Rubin**, its next generation. ([investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2025/NVIDIA-Blackwell-Ultra-AI-Factory-Platform-Paves-Way-for-Age-of-AI-Reasoning/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

- **Blackwell Ultra:** Nvidia said partner systems such as the **GB300 NVL72** would be available in the **second half of 2025**. The upgrade offered more computing power and up to **288 GB of high-bandwidth memory per GPU**, aimed at speeding up AI training and running reasoning models. ([investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2025/NVIDIA-Blackwell-Ultra-AI-Factory-Platform-Paves-Way-for-Age-of-AI-Reasoning/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))
- **Vera Rubin:** Nvidia said systems pairing the new **Rubin GPU** with the **Vera CPU** were planned for the **second half of 2026**, with **Rubin Ultra** to follow in the **second half of 2027**. ([nvidia.com](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/on-demand/session/gtc25-s72484/?utm_source=openai))

Later, on **September 9, 2025**, Nvidia also announced **Rubin CPX**, a specialized GPU for processing very long inputs in workloads like coding and video generation. It was expected at the **end of 2026**. ([nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-unveils-rubin-cpx-a-new-class-of-gpu-designed-for-massive-context-inference?trk=public_post_comment-text&utm_source=openai))
